summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:
- **ASFA / SSA Title IV-E** — court findings; timelines; permanency planning  
- **CFSR (45 CFR Part 1355)** — federal review of court/agency performance measures

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services v. Michelle P.
key_cases.holding: CINA jurisdiction derives from the child's status as a child in need of aid and is distinct from a custody or supervision grant, so dismissal of the petition was reversed; separately, the removal order was vacated because it lacked sufficient evidentiary support and did not satisfy ICWA.
key_cases.relevance: Reverses a dismissal of a CINA petition and explains what keeps the dependency case open.
key_cases.quote: This was error because the removal order was not supported by sufficient evidence and did not comply with the requirements of the Indian Child Welfare Act (ICWA).

key_cases.case_name: Payton S. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Although the parents did not receive the notice required before the adjudication and disposition hearing, the defect did not affect the outcome and so did not deprive them of due process; the termination was affirmed on the evidence.
key_cases.relevance: States the notice parents and tribes are owed once a CINA petition proceeds to adjudication and disposition.
key_cases.quote: CINA Rule 15(b) requires that parents and other interested parties in an ICWA proceeding receive notice of an adjudication hearing "at least ten days before the hearing"

key_cases.case_name: Amy S. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Assuming without deciding that the superior court violated due process by taking judicial notice of contested facts, pleadings, and testimony from the parents' domestic-relations file when adjudicating the child in need of aid, any error was harmless, and the adjudication was affirmed.
key_cases.relevance: Governs the evidentiary basis on which a court may adjudicate a child in need of aid after a petition is filed.
key_cases.quote: taking judicial notice of the existence of ten years of custody disputes is different than taking judicial notice of specific facts, pleadings, and testimony from the custody case

key_cases.case_name: Rowan B. v. State, Department of Health & Social Services, Office of Children's Services
key_cases.holding: Civil discovery rules, not the Public Records Act exemptions, govern a CINA parent's request for law-enforcement records, and the trial court erred by denying the request outright instead of conducting an in camera review.
key_cases.relevance: Establishes that Alaska Civil Rules 26-37 and 45 apply once a CINA petition is filed.
key_cases.quote: We hold that the trial court erred in denying Rowan access to materials he sought through discovery without at least conducting an in camera review.

key_cases.case_name: Office of Public Advocacy v. Superior Court, Third Judicial District
key_cases.holding: A putative father's parentage may be established in a CINA proceeding on legally sufficient non-genetic evidence, so CINA Rule 2(k)'s definition of "parent" — and the party status and appointed counsel that follow — reaches a person the superior court determines to be a parent without scientific testing.
key_cases.relevance: Determines who becomes a party entitled to counsel and notice once OCS files a CINA petition, the threshold question for every downstream procedural right.
key_cases.quote: We conclude that a judicial determination of paternity does not necessarily need underlying scientific, genetic testing in this context

timeline_requirements.requirement_name: Child in need of aid petition filed after emergency custody
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: If the child is released instead, the department must file a report with the court within 24 hours of the release (AS 47.10.142(c))
Statute sets no penalty; the court may continue the hearing for good cause, taking into account the child's age and the adverse effect of delay (AS 47.10.080(a))
